# opnsense_caddy_header (Resource)

Header manipulation rules for Caddy handlers (**Services ▸ Caddy Web Server ▸ Reverse Proxy ▸ Headers**, plugin `os-caddy`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opnsense_caddy_header" "real_ip" {
  header = "X-Real-IP"
  value  = "{remote_host}"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `header` (String) Enter a header, for example "Host". Use the "+" or "-" prefix to add or remove this header, for example "-Host" or "+Host". A suffix match like "-Host-*" is also supported. To replace a header, use "Host" without "+" or "-".

### Optional

- `description` (String) Enter a description for this header. Defaults to ``.
- `direction` (String) "header_up" sets, adds (with the "+" prefix), deletes (with the "-" prefix), or performs a replacement (by using two arguments, a search and replacement) in a request header going upstream to the backend. "header_down" sets, adds (with the "+" prefix), deletes (with the "-" prefix), or performs a replacement (by using two arguments, a search and replacement) in a response header coming downstream from the backend. One of `header_up`, `header_down`. Defaults to `header_up`.
- `replace` (String) If a regular expression is used to search for a Header Value, the replacement string can be set here. For example: "replaced-$1-suffix" which expands the replacement string, allowing the use of captured values, "$1" being the first capture group. Defaults to ``.
- `value` (String) Enter a value for the selected header. One of the most common options is "{upstream_hostport}". It is also possible to use a regular expression to search for a specific value in a header. For example: "^prefix-([A-Za-z0-9]*)$" which uses the regular expression language RE2 included in Go. Defaults to ``.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the Caddy header rule.
